cards.explanation: The answer is haughty. That's the word the LORD uses. He says the daughters of Zion are haughty, walking with heads held high and wanton eyes (Isaiah 3:16). Isaiah is the prophet passing along the LORD's words here. Heads held high, prancing and skipping, and a humble step nowhere in the picture.

The answer is that they will be struck with sores. Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, the Lord will bring sores on their heads (Isaiah 3:17). Those heads were held high, and now they get sores. This is a hard line, so I'll just say it plainly and move on.

The answer is True. Right after the sores, the verse says the LORD will make their foreheads bare (Isaiah 3:17). It's one sentence of the Lord's warning, and it's a heavy one. I think this part stings, so we'll let it be.

The answer is that fine things become lowly things. Every swap goes down. Instead of fragrance, a stench. Instead of a belt, a rope. Instead of fine clothing, sackcloth (Isaiah 3:24). The nice thing is traded for the lowly thing every single time.
The answer is sackcloth. The verse says, "instead of fine clothing, sackcloth…" (Isaiah 3:24). Sackcloth is rough, plain cloth. That's a long way down from a festive robe.
The answer is True. The last swap on the list is "instead of beauty, shame." (Isaiah 3:24). It's the end of the string of swaps, and it lands hard. I think this one is the heaviest of them.

The answer is that the gates lament and mourn. "And the gates of Zion will lament and mourn…" (Isaiah 3:26). It comes right after the men and warriors fall in the verse before. I think that's one of the saddest pictures in this passage.
The answer is False. Isaiah says, "destitute, she will sit on the ground." (Isaiah 3:26). Zion is down on the ground, not standing tall.

The answer is that they want to be called by his name. The women say, "Just let us be called by your name. Take away our disgrace!" (Isaiah 4:1). They'll even eat their own bread and provide their own clothes. His name is what they want to carry.

The answer is beautiful and glorious. That's how Isaiah describes the Branch of the LORD. "On that day the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious…" (Isaiah 4:2). After all those swaps going down, here's a word going up. Hold onto this one, friends.

The answer is False. The fruit of the land "…will be the pride and glory of Israel’s survivors." (Isaiah 4:2). Here it's their pride and glory, not something taken away. After so much being taken away, this verse is a relief.

The answer is True, friends. Isaiah says, "Whoever remains in Zion and whoever is left in Jerusalem will be called holy…" (Isaiah 4:3). That includes all in Jerusalem who are recorded among the living. Holy is a good word to end up with.

The answer is that He washes and cleanses them away. The Lord has "…washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and cleansed the bloodstains from the heart of Jerusalem…" (Isaiah 4:4). It's washing and cleansing, and it's done by the Lord. Both the filth and the bloodstains are dealt with.
The answer is True. The cleansing comes "…by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire." (Isaiah 4:4). Those are the words Isaiah uses. The Lord is the one doing the cleansing.
The answer is a glowing flame of fire. "…a cloud of smoke by day and a glowing flame of fire by night." (Isaiah 4:5). Smoke in the daytime, flame at night. The LORD creates both over Mount Zion.

The answer is heat. The canopy is "…a shelter to give shade from the heat by day…" (Isaiah 4:6). It's also a refuge and hiding place from the storm and the rain. Shade in the day and cover in the storm.
